{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '<file name="D:\\dev\\ab-tasks\\_briefs\\raptor\\brief.md">\n# Task Brief: Port Raptor: Call of the Shadows (Sector 1) to HTML5\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nPort *Raptor: Call of the Shadows* (Apogee, 1994) — sector 1 only, the shareware\ncontent — from the original DOS game to a browser game built with HTML5 canvas,\nvanilla JavaScript, and the Web Audio API. The port must render real game assets\n(graphics and sounds) extracted from the original shareware data files, either at\nbuild time or at runtime — no placeholder art, no placeholder audio. Do not use\nany external frameworks or libraries beyond what ships in the browser (no React,\nPhaser, PixiJS, Howler, etc.). A small vanilla test runner is fine if you want\none, but it is not required.\n\n## 2. Worktree Layout\n\nYour worktree root (`./`) contains the GPL C/ASM source of the original DOS game,\nprovided for reference and porting purposes, under `SOURCE/`, `GFX/`, `audiolib/`,\nand `apodmx/`. It also contains the original shareware game data files under\n`./data/` — GLB archive files, the shareware `RAP.EXE` for reference, and whatever\nelse the shareware distribution contained.\n\nBuild your web port as new files alongside/above this existing tree (for example\n`index.html`, an asset-extraction or build script, and your JS source), and keep\nthe original source tree intact for reference — do not delete or rewrite it.\n\nYou must write and maintain a `README` documenting a working dev-server command\n(for example `npx serve .`, `python -m http.server`, or similar) so that the port\ncan be opened and played in a browser at any milestone. Keep this command accurate\nand working as you go — it will be used to check your progress at each milestone.\n\n## 3. Standing Rules\n\n- Vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 canvas + Web Audio API only. No external runtime\n  frameworks or libraries. A lightweight bundler or dev-only tool is fine if it\n  produces plain output, but avoid dependency-heavy tooling.\n- Always leave behind a documented, working dev server command that serves a\n  working build.\n- Commit to git after completing each milestone (M1 through M5, below), so\n  progress is checkpointed.\n- Sector 1 (shareware) content only — you do not need to support later sectors\n  or the registered/full game.\n\n## 4. Milestone Ladder (M1–M5)\n\nThis is the actual grading spec. Copied verbatim:\n\n- **M1**: level-1 background + player ship rendered on canvas from the real GLB\n  data. Graded by screenshot similarity (SSIM) to a reference DOSBox frame on the\n  playfield region (target >= 0.80), and >= 90% of the reference color palette\n  present.\n- **M2**: arrow keys move the ship; firing spawns a projectile.\n- **M3**: wave-1 enemies spawn; a projectile hit decrements enemy HP or removes\n  the enemy; the player can die.\n- **M4**: HUD (score/shields) renders; a Web Audio context is running and at\n  least one sound effect is triggered on firing.\n- **M5**: the sector-1 loop completes — the wave counter advances through wave 9\n  and a sector-complete screen appears.\n\n## 5. Grader Interface Contract\n\nYou **must** implement exactly this. An automated Playwright script checks\nagainst it — this is a hard requirement, not a suggestion.\n\n- A canvas element `<canvas id="raptor-canvas">` whose internal pixel buffer is\n  exactly 320x200 (`canvas.width === 320`, `canvas.height === 200`), independent\n  of any CSS display scaling.\n- Controls: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` / `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` move the ship;\n  the Space bar fires. Use standard `keydown`/`keyup` DOM listeners — no custom\n  input hook needed.\n- A live-updated global object `window.__raptor` with this exact shape:\n\n  ```js\n  window.__raptor = {\n    ready: boolean,            // true once the first frame (background + player ship) is drawn from real game data\n    player: { x: number, y: number, alive: boolean },\n    projectiles: [ { x: number, y: number, owner: \'player\'|\'enemy\' }, /* ... */ ],\n    enemies: [ { id: string|number, hp: number, x: number, y: number, alive: boolean }, /* ... */ ],\n    hud: { score: number, shields: number },\n    audio: { contextState: \'running\'|\'suspended\'|\'closed\', sfxCount: number },  // sfxCount increments on every SFX triggered\n    wave: number,               // current wave within sector 1\n    sectorComplete: boolean\n  };\n  ```\n\n- Keep this object\'s fields in sync with actual game state at all times. The\n  grader polls it, drives real keyboard input to test M2/M3/M4/M5, and takes a\n  canvas screenshot to test M1. For M5 the grader is allowed to auto-play (hold\n  fire, jitter movement) rather than requiring skilled play, so you do not need\n  to build any special "autoplay" or "god mode" feature — just make the interface\n  accurately reflect real game state during ordinary play.\n\n</file>\n'}], 'attribution': 'user', 'timestamp': 1787283951008}

The key items for the game:\n\n- FILE0000.GLB: text, music, SFX (Apogee Sound System format — .APF? Actually it\'s the old Apogee sound format: a header of 52 bytes containing rate, volume, loop, type, data)\n- FILE0001.GLB:\n  - 0x10000: palette (768 bytes of VGA palette)\n  - 0x10001: SYSTEM_FNT font\n  - 0x10022: BACKGRND_PIC — background image!\n  - Fonts, numbers (N0-N9, N$), SHLDLOW_PIC (shields low?)\n  - SPRITE1_ITM (0x100fc) — sprite library (SPRITE array)\n  - FLATSG1_ITM (0x100fd) — flat library (FLATS array)\n  - MAP1G1_MAP..MAP9G1_MAP (0x100fe-0x10106) — 9 waves of MAZELEVEL data!\n  - SHIP01G1_PIC.. — sprite graphics (GFX_PIC)\n  - STARTG1TILES..ENDG1TILES label — ground tiles (flat graphics)\n\nSo the "waves" are literally 9 MAP files (MAP1G1_MAP - MAP9G1_MAP) — 9 waves per sector! This matches M5\'s "the wave counter advances through wave 9".\n\nThe MAZELEVEL struct contains `map[MAP_SIZE]`, where MAP_SIZE = 150*9 = 1350 MAZEDATA entries, each 4 bytes (2 shorts) = 5400 bytes + 12-byte header. Each MAZEDATA: flats index, fgame.\n\nWait, but MAP_ROWS=150, MAP_COLS=9: the map is a scrolling vertical strip. The playfield is 320x200, and the map scrolls downward (the player flies upward). The visible area is 8x9 = 72 cells? MAP_ONSCREEN=8, MAP_COLS=9. Each cell is 32x32 px. 9 cols * 32 = 288 px = MAP_RIGHT-MAP_LEFT (304-16=288). 8 rows * 32 = 256 > 200-18… hmm, MAP_BOTTOM=182, MAP_TOP=2, height 180 px.\n\nLet me look at RAP.C\'s Do_Game and ENEMY.C to understand wave loading and spawning. The MAZEDATA.flats field references an index into flatlib (FLATS array). FLATS.linkflat is a link to the next cell in the same flat group? Let me actually read ENEMY_C to understand.\n\nAlso, I need to understand how the map scrolls: the game has a "map" that scrolls down as the player advances. The MAP1G1 map has 150 rows of 9 columns. The 8 rows on screen. The top row of the visible window advances with the player\'s y position? Encrypt Data\r\n ***************************************************************************/\r\nVOID\r\nGLB_EnCrypt(\r\nCHAR     *key,             // INPUT : Key that will allow Decryption\r\nBYTE     *buffer,          // INPUT : Buffer to Encrypt\r\nsize_t   length            // INPUT : Length of Buffer\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   INT   klen = strlen( key );\r\n   INT   prev_byte;\r\n   INT   kidx;\r\n  \r\n   kidx = SEED % klen;\r\n   prev_byte = key[ kidx ];\r\n   while ( length-- )\r\n   {\r\n      prev_byte = ( *buffer + key[ kidx ] + prev_byte ) % 256;\r\n      *buffer++ = prev_byte;\r\n  \r\n      if ( ++kidx >= klen )\r\n         kidx = 0;\r\n   }\r\n}\r\n  \r\n/***************************************************************************\r\n  GLB_DeCrypt - Decrypt Data\r\n ***************************************************************************/\r\nVOID\r\nGLB_DeCrypt(\r\nCHAR    *key,               // INPUT : Key that will allow Decryption\r\nBYTE    *buffer,            // INPUT : Buffer to Encrypt\r\nsize_t  length              // INPUT : Length of Buffer\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   INT   klen = strlen( key );\r\n   INT   prev_byte;\r\n   INT   kidx;\r\n   CHAR  dchr;\r\n  \r\n   kidx = SEED % klen;\r\n   prev_byte = key[ kidx ];\r\n   while ( length-- )\r\n   {\r\n      dchr = ( *buffer - key[ kidx ] - prev_byte ) % 256;\r\n      prev_byte = *buffer;\r\n      *buffer++ = dchr;\r\n  \r\n      if ( ++kidx >= klen )\r\n         kidx = 0;\r\n   }\r\n}\r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_FindFile() - Finds a file, opens it, and stores it\'s path \r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_FindFile(\r\nINT\treturn_on_failure,\t// INPUT : Don\'t bomb if file not open\r\nINT\tfilenum,             // INPUT : file number\r\nINT\tpermissions\t\t\t\t// INPUT : file access permissions\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   char        *routine = "GLB_FindFile";\r\n   char        filename[ _MAX_PATH ];\r\n   int         handle;\r\n   FILEDESC    *fd;\r\n/*\r\n* Scott, the ASSERT function is a macro that will be compiled-out when\r\n* not debugging ( DEBUG not defined ), otherwise it calls EXIT_Assert\r\n* if the expression is false ( which bails out of your program and displays\r\n* the expression, file & line number of the assertion ).  This is a standard\r\n* way of checking variables for correct boundries during development, and\r\n* makes it easy to remove extra logic for doing so by recompiling without\r\n* DEBUG defined.\r\n*/\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < MAX_GLB_FILES );\r\n/*\r\n* create a file name and attempt to open it local first, then if it\r\n* fails use the exe path and try again.\r\n*/\r\n   sprintf( filename, "%s%04u.glb", prefix, filenum );\r\n   if ( ( handle = open( filename, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t{\r\n      sprintf( filename, "%s%s%04u.glb", exePath, prefix, filenum );\r\n   \tif ( ( handle = open( filename, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t\t{\r\n\t\t\tif ( return_on_failure )\r\n\t\t\t\treturn -1;\r\n\r\n         sprintf( filename, "%s%04u.glb", prefix, filenum );\r\n   \t   EXIT_Error ("GLB_FindFile: %s, Error #%d,%s",\r\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfilename, errno, strerror( errno ) );\r\n\t\t}\r\n\t}\r\n/*\r\n* Keep file handle\r\n*/\r\n   fd = &filedesc[ filenum ];\r\n\r\n   strcpy( fd->filepath, filename );\r\n   fd->permissions = permissions;\r\n   fd->handle = handle;\r\n\r\n\treturn handle;\r\n}\r\n  \r\n\r\n  \r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_OpenFile() - Opens & Caches file handle\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_OpenFile(\r\nINT\treturn_on_failure,\t// INPUT : Don\'t bomb if file not open\r\nINT\tfilenum,             // INPUT : file number\r\nINT\tpermissions\t\t\t\t// INPUT : file access permissions\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   FILEDESC    *fd;\r\n\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < MAX_GLB_FILES );\r\n\r\n   fd = &filedesc[ filenum ];\r\n\r\n   if ( fd->handle == 0 )\r\n      return GLB_FindFile( return_on_failure, filenum, permissions );\r\n   else if ( fd->permissions != permissions )\r\n   {\r\n      close( fd->handle );\r\n   \tif ( ( fd->handle = open( fd->filepath, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t\t{\r\n\t\t\tif ( return_on_failure )\r\n\t\t\t\treturn -1;\r\n\r\n   \t   EXIT_Error ("GLB_OpenFile: %s, Error #%d,%s",\r\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfd->filepath, errno, strerror( errno ) );\r\n      }\r\n   }\r\n   else\r\n   {\r\n      lseek( fd->handle, 0L, SEEK_SET );\r\n   }\r\n   return fd->handle;\r\n}\r\n  \r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_CloseFiles() - Closes all cached files.\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE VOID\r\nGLB_CloseFiles(\r\nVOID\r\n)\r\n{\r\n\tINT\t\tj;\r\n\r\n\tfor ( j = 0; j < MAX_GLB_FILES; j++ )\r\n\t{\r\n      if ( filedesc[ j ].handle )\r\n      {\r\n   \t\tclose( filedesc[ j ].handle );\r\n         filedesc[ j ].handle = 0;\r\n      }\r\n\t}\r\n}\r\n\r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_NumItems() - Returns number of items in a .GLB file\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_NumItems (\r\nINT filenum\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   KEYFILE     key;\r\n   INT         handle;\r\n\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < num_glbs );\r\n\r\n\thandle = GLB_OpenFile( 1, filenum, O_RDONLY | O_BINARY );\r\n\tif ( handle == -1 )\r\n\t\treturn 0;\r\n\r\n   lseek( handle, 0L, SEEK_SET );\r\n   if ( ! read( handle,( VOID * ) &key, sizeof( KEYFILE ) ) )\r\n   {\r\n      EXIT_Error( "GLB_NumItems: Read failed!" );\r\n   }\r\n  \r\n#ifdef _SCOTTGAME\r\n   GLB_DeCrypt( serial, ( BYTE * )&key, sizeof( KEYFILE ) );\r\n#endif\r\n  \r\n   return ( ( int ) key.offset );\r\n}\r\n\r\n/*--------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n GLB_LoadIDT() Loads a item descriptor table from a GLB file.\r\n --------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE VOID\r\nGLB_LoadIDT(\r\nFILEDESC *fd               // INPUT: file to load\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   int      handle;\r\n   int      j;\r\n\tint\t\tk;\r\n\tint \t\tn;\r\n   KEYFILE  key[ 10 ];\r\n   ITEMINFO *ii;\r\n\r\n   handle = fd->handle;\r\n   ii = fd->item;\r\n\r\n   lseek( handle, sizeof( KEYFILE ), SEEK_SET );\r', 'truncated': True, 'truncatedBy': 'lines', 'totalLines': 860, 'totalBytes': 7803, 'outputLines': 300, 'outputBytes': 7803, 'lastLinePartial': False, 'firstLineExceedsLimit': False}, 'totalLines': 860, 'displayContent': {'text': '/****************************************************************************\r\n* GLBapi  -
